scores.evidence: Checked runs/tier3/extracts/*.json and runs/tier3/brief.json against the four sources in fixtures/northlight_01/. What holds up: every anchor I checked is verbatim and on the right line (for example transcript_kickoff [00:03:41] 'our buyer is 25 to 40, urban professionals', rfp_meltemi '## 6. Προϋπολογισμός'). All three cross-source conflicts are captured with both sides cited (audiences, budget, and timeline with 4 positions). The retracted metro OOH idea is absent. The TikTok dance idea is carried as conditional/low. Open questions cover KPIs, approver, formats and the ingredient list. The garbled tokens are kept as-is in the extract with extraction_notes (transcript_kickoff.json extraction_notes[0..1]). harness_report.json shows 17/17, and the pytest suite runs 587 passed / 16 xfailed. Known weaknesses on the second fixture are documented honestly in runs/voreas_prep_report.md (dropped garble-flagged objective, superseded date asserted, render-stage 'hero' invention, duplicate questions) and in docs/DEMO_PLAYBOOK.md:94-103. But the canonical brief still has content-level defects that the harness cannot see.
defects: The budget hedge drifts, against skills/SYNTHESIS.md rule 2, which itself uses 'κάπου στα ογδόντα' -> 'around eighty (units unstated)' as the example. brief.json conflicts[1].positions[1].statement says 'somewhere in the eighties, maybe eighty-five'. The resolution and the signoff.edits_summary say 'Production budget in the eighties'. 'In the eighties' means a range of 80-89 and drops 'units unstated'. The open question in the same brief says 'around eighty' correctly, so the brief contradicts itself on its most sensitive figure.

One claim is attributed to the wrong source. key_messages[3] reads 'the key visual should evoke summer, but premium summer — not a generic beach-party feel' and cites only transcript_kickoff [00:06:02]. The beach-party clause comes from background_brand_guidelines §Category no-gos; Dimitris never said it. The cited source gets a clause it never wrote. SYNTHESIS forbids this; the verbatim gates cannot see it.

Garbled terms are resolved silently in what the reader sees. objectives[2] content and both renders say 'brand awareness' / 'key visual'. The ASR tokens «μπραντ αγουέρνες» / «κι βίζουαλ» survive only inside evidence anchors (grep finds 0 hits in brief_el.md and brief_en.md), and no interpretation note reaches the reader. docs/EVIDENCE.md:50 claims they were 'carried as-is through extract → brief → renders … never silently corrected'. That overstates it: harness T3.3 passes only because the anchor strings sit inside brief.json (eval/harness.py:481).

After sign-off, the resolved values do not appear in their own fields. audiences, budget and timeline carry no entry for 25–40, production ~80 excl. media, or 15 September. Those values exist only in the conflicts[] resolutions. The renders therefore say 'No confirmed entries' for Audiences and Budget, and the open questions still ask the client to decide the audience (#2) and 'the definitive launch date' (#9), which the account lead has already settled.

Fields are misclassified. deliverables[0] ('Final approval of the brief is a required step') and deliverables[1] ('Northlight will send a revised plan') are agency process steps, not campaign deliverables. The approver gap is filed under field 'mandatories'. Tone-of-voice guidance is filed under key_messages.

A material strategic gap is missing. RFP §4's TikTok-first mandate was written alongside the Gen Z 18–24 audience that the CMO withdrew at [00:03:41]. The brief never asks whether TikTok-first still holds for a 25–40 urban-professional buyer. Open question #8 asks what TikTok-first means but does not link it to the audience correction.

The extraction translated despite SOURCES.md rule 5. transcript_kickoff.json key_messages[0].value renders 'φυσικά υλικά' as 'natural ingredients', and key_messages[1] is an English paraphrase, while the neighbouring budget value stays in Greek.
scores.to_reach_9: Re-roll synthesis on the tier3 extracts with three spec lines added. First, carry the hedge verbatim in meaning ('around eighty, maybe eighty-five (units unstated)') and never write 'in the eighties'. Second, one entry cites only the sources whose words it uses, with no cross-source clauses. Third, agency process steps become open questions, not deliverables. Add a runner-side post-sign-off step that writes each resolved conflict position into its field as a cited entry and retires open questions whose field has a resolved conflict. Carry garble interpretation visibly, e.g. 'brand awareness (ASR: «μπραντ αγουέρνες», glossary match)'. Correct docs/EVIDENCE.md:50 to describe what actually reaches the renders. Add an open question linking TikTok-first to the audience correction.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/brief_el.md and brief_en.md side by side against skills/TRANSLATION.md and glossary/meltemi.json. What works: the two renders match item for item. Protected Latin terms are intact (Meltemi Fizz, key visual, brand awareness, launch, KPI, media spend). The conditional hedge appears in both ('Υπό συζήτηση — δεν έχει επιβεβαιωθεί' / 'Conditional — under discussion, not confirmed'). The Greek largely reads as real agency register with natural code-switching ('Βασικό μηνυματικό angle', 'σε λογική premium-everyday'). For an account lead to send it, though, the Greek has several grammar and agreement errors, most of them in the client-facing questions, and both renders carry contradictions and internal metadata.
defects: The client-facing Greek questions have grammar errors that a Greek client would notice. brief_el.md:54 'η θέση της προσώπου' should be 'του προσώπου'. Line 66 'Ποιό' takes no accent on the monosyllable: 'Ποιο'. Line 78 'που ακριβώς θα χρησιμοποιηθούν' is the interrogative, so 'πού'. Line 86 'τη τελική έγκριση' should be 'την τελική'. Line 68 'τη κατηγορία' should be 'την κατηγορία'.

Gender and case errors elsewhere. brief_el.md:103 'σύμφωνα με τον CFO' refers to Anna, so it should be 'την CFO'. Line 95 'ορίζει το κοινό-στόχος ως' should be 'το κοινό-στόχο'. Line 103 'Ο προϋπολογισμός media διαχειρίζεται ξεχωριστά' says the budget manages; it should be 'Τη διαχείριση του media budget την κάνει ξεχωριστά ο media shop του πελάτη'. Line 115 'Επιλύθηκαν οι τρεις αντικρούσεις' uses αντίκρουση (rebuttal) where 'συγκρούσεις/αντιφάσεις' is meant.

The figure is not equivalent across the two renders. EN :102-103 and :115 say 'in the eighties'. EL :102-103 say 'κάπου στα ογδόντα' / 'στα ογδόντα' ('around eighty'). The two languages now state different budget ranges.

Both renders contradict themselves. The heading '⚠ Unresolved Conflicts (account lead must resolve before sign-off)' / '⚠ Ανεπίλυτες Συγκρούσεις' (EN :92, EL :92, fixed in templates/northlight_client_brief.md:34) sits over three items marked 'resolved by human'. Under a SIGNED OFF banner, open questions #2 and #9 still ask the client to settle the audience and launch date.

Terms are used inconsistently, with some calques. Line 3 says 'επικεφαλής λογαριασμού' while lines 92 and 115 use 'account lead'. 'Κάλυψη εισερχομένων', 'καταχωρήσεις' and 'εγκριτή' are system calques, not agency Greek. 'Το Northlight θα στείλει' reads better with the feminine company article, 'Η Northlight'.

It is not ready to send. A document titled 'Client Brief' exposes internal pipeline metadata to the client (Sensitivity tier S1, 'Input coverage 5/7', 'Verdict: Ready for review', 'Pipeline: brief-builder-stage1'). The EN suggested question keeps 'today it was said' from a question drafted on the day of the kickoff.

The problem is broader than one run. The second-fixture render runs/voreas-prep-03/brief_el.md shows the same class: raw enums in the header ('[RENDER_LANG: EL]', 'Verdict: ready_for_review', 'advertising_creative') and the transliteration 'στέντ' for 'stand'. skills/TRANSLATION.md §4 has no Greek grammar or gender self-check, and no gate covers Greek language quality.
scores.to_reach_9: Add a Greek language self-check to skills/TRANSLATION.md §4 covering four things: article-noun agreement and final -ν before vowels and plosives, gender of named people taken from the transcript's participant line, accents on ποιο/πού, and one fixed rendering per role term. Add a small deterministic Greek lint to the render gate for the known-bad patterns listed above. Make the conflicts heading conditional on status in the template. Move internal metadata into a clearly labelled internal footer. Then re-render tier3 and commit the corrected EL/EN renders as the new evidence pack, with a before/after diff.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/creative/creative_brief_sonnet.md and creative_brief_opus.md against brief.json and config/channel_specs.json. What works: both drafts follow the 8-section skeleton. Both carry a truthful 'SHADOW MODE — evaluation draft. Not for delivery.' banner. Mandatories are copied verbatim. Every spec token matches a table row byte-for-byte with its row id (tiktok_infeed_video 9:16 1080x1920 9-60s MP4; key_visual_digital_master 1:1 2048x2048 PNG). Opus handles YouTube correctly with 'SPEC NOT IN TABLE — ask traffic/production' and lists the Instagram rows only as available, not committed. Sonnet declines to invent a platform. The readiness checklists are the strongest part: specific, cited, split into blocking and non-blocking items. The weak points are strategic sharpness and fact discipline, and runs/tier_4_report.md:65 overstates the result as 'differ in thoroughness, not correctness — both are trap-clean'.
defects: Sonnet invents currency and scale. creative_brief_sonnet.md:64 and :69 give 'Production budget: "in the eighties" (€80–85k)'. The brief's own open question says the unit and currency are unconfirmed, and SYNTHESIS rule 2 forbids €/thousands. This is exactly the conversion that docs/DECK.md:122 claims never happens ('No €80,000 appears anywhere'). X3 and the creative spec gate check neither the creative drafts nor currency tokens.

The drafts invent facts. Sonnet :9 says sparkling tea is 'a category … that is new to Greece'; the source says new for the company ('καινούργια κατηγορία για εμάς', transcript [00:02:05]). Opus :11 says 'the Greek-made sparkling tea', a place-of-manufacture claim that no source makes ('ελληνικό brand' ≠ Greek-made). A claims reviewer would strike it. Both breach the agent's rule 3, 'Nothing enters that is not in the brief'.
Opus :73 calls the TikTok dance 'retracted'. It was hedged ('don't hold me to it'), not retracted.

Neither draft engages the brief's central strategic tensions. First, a TikTok-first mandate written for Gen Z now serves a 25–40 urban-professional buyer. Second, a launch on 15 September at the end of the season meets a key visual that must 'shout premium summer'. The SMPs are competent category statements, not sharp choices. Opus RTB 4 ('Premium-summer, not generic beach party') is a visual direction, not a reason to believe.

The tone mandatory is 'Confident, modern Greek with natural use of English category terms', yet both drafts are English-only. There is no Greek-language line, territory or example of the code-switched register for a Greek creative team to react to.

The committed drafts no longer match the current creative contract in .claude/agents/creative-shadow.md §4-5 (a 'CREATIVE DRAFT' banner and canonical '[brief:objectives:0]' citations). They use loose tags such as '[key_messages, transcript_kickoff 00:06:02]'. No refreshed draft under the Tier-6 release contract is committed as evidence.
scores.to_reach_9: Extend pipeline/creative.py check_creative_brief with a fact-trace check that fails a draft when any currency mark or figure is absent from brief content strings. Add origin/market terms ('Greek-made', 'new to Greece') to the creative lint as a flag for human review. Add one line to the creative-shadow skeleton asking for 'Strategic tensions the brief leaves open' and one Greek example line in the brand register. Regenerate the A/B under the current contract. Correct runs/tier_4_report.md §3 to record the €80–85k, 'new to Greece' and 'Greek-made' findings.

They show 'No confirmed entries' for Audiences and Budget, and they still ask the client for the audience and launch date. That is the single most visible defect for an account lead sending the document.

Add regression tests using the tier3 strings. Re-roll the synthesis conflict statement so it reads 'around eighty, maybe eighty-five (units unstated)'.

moves.rationale: The renders silently show 'brand awareness' / 'key visual', and the garbled tokens survive only in JSON anchors. docs/EVIDENCE.md:50 claims they were carried as-is through the renders. An account lead cannot tell that a glossary interpretation happened.

Both are English-only despite a Greek tone mandatory, and the committed drafts predate the current CREATIVE DRAFT banner and canonical-citation contract.

Strategic tensions — contradictions or premises the brief leaves open, each citing the entries in tension' and require one example line in the brand's Greek register under Tone. pipeline/creative.py: flag origin/market qualifiers (Greek-made, new to Greece/market, first, only) for human review unless they occur in brief content. moves.title: Synthesis field hygiene: one source per clause, process steps out of deliverables, premise-change questions
moves.rationale: key_messages[3] attributes a brand-guidelines clause to the CMO's transcript line. Brief approval and the revised plan sit under deliverables. The brief never asks whether TikTok-first survives the audience correction.
moves.concrete_changes: skills/SYNTHESIS.md: add three one-sentence rules. (1) An entry's content uses only words supported by its cited evidence; a clause from another source needs that source's evidence ref or its own entry. (2) Agency process commitments (approvals, revised plans) are not deliverables; raise them as open questions. (3) When a conflict position that another entry was premised on (e.g. the Gen Z audience behind TikTok-first) is superseded, raise an open question linking the two. Re-roll synthesis on the tier3 extracts; add regression assertions to tests/test_regression_voreas.py-style fixtures for northlight.

moves.title: Separate client-facing render from internal metadata
moves.rationale: A document titled 'Client Brief' shows the client the sensitivity tier, input coverage, readiness verdict and pipeline version. Greek calques such as 'Κάλυψη εισερχομένων' make it read like a system export.
moves.concrete_changes: templates/northlight_client_brief.md: move Sensitivity tier / Input coverage / Verdict / Pipeline / Generated into a trailing '— Internal (not for client) —' block, or drop them from client renders and keep them in brief_review.html. skills/TRANSLATION.md: fix the Greek labels ('Κάλυψη πεδίων με τεκμηρίωση', 'Αξιολόγηση ετοιμότητας'). Re-render and commit.

overall: The evidence layer is strong for an MVP. Citations are verbatim and correctly placed, every seeded conflict and gap is caught, the conditional and retracted traps are handled, and channel specs are genuinely table-bound. Weaknesses on the second fixture are documented candidly. Output quality as a senior bilingual strategist would receive it is weaker than the 17/17 harness suggests. The canonical brief lets a spoken hedge drift ('in the eighties'), and one creative draft turns it into €80–85k. A brand-guidelines clause is attributed to the CMO's line. The signed-off renders contradict themselves (an 'Unresolved Conflicts' heading over resolved items, empty Audience and Budget sections, questions re-asking settled points). The client-facing Greek has repeated article, gender and accent errors. The creative drafts invent origin and market claims and miss the brief's two real strategic tensions. None of this needs frozen files changed. It needs a few spec lines in SYNTHESIS, TRANSLATION and creative-shadow, runner-side lints, and a re-render of the tier3 evidence. Side note: an untracked runs/tier3/.run.lock appeared in the working tree during this review; it was not created by this judge.
